 Live Updates Updated Tue, Nov 3 2026 2:17 PM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Nasdaq rebounds as chip stocks bounce, Dow dragged lower by Apple: Live updates
 Sean Conlon Deena Zaidi Lim Hui Jie Traders work at the New York Stock Exchange on Nov. 2, 2026. NYSE The Nasdaq Composite rose on Tuesday as investors moved back into key technology stocks after recent pressure and geared up for U.S. midterm election results .
 The tech-heavy index jumped 1.1%, recouping some of its latest losses. The Nasdaq-100 also rose 0.9% but still traded in correction territory, still down about 10% from its recent high. The S&P 500 climbed 0.6%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average traded down 100 points, or 0.2%, weighed down by Apple shares.
 Apple fell almost 2% after the iPhone maker issued a disappointing margin forecast late Monday and iPad sales in the fiscal fourth-quarter missed the Street's estimates.
 Conversely, shares of chipmakers saw gains. Advanced Micro Devices — which releases its third-quarter results after the bell — gained 4%, while Broadcom rose more than 3%. Micron Technology and Nvidia each added more than 2%.
 Tuesday's advance marks a reversal from the pullback seen Monday, which sent the Nasdaq down more than 1% and extended a recent retreat in the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 to a third day. 
 While semiconductor makers — and others tied to artificial intelligence — showed signs of recovery Tuesday, Shawn Snyder of Potomac Fund Management believes the market is not out of the woods.
 "The concerns about the cost of capital and the level of debt financing necessary [are] going to persist for quite some time," the economic strategist told CNBC. But the trade that relies on the artificial intelligence buildout could be getting close to oversold territory, he added, saying that "maybe there's a little bit more downside, 4% or 5%, but eventually, if there's not a recession associated with these drawdowns, normally that's kind of where it stops."
 Oil prices, meanwhile, turned lower on speculation there might be progress in U.S.-Iran negotiations. Brent crude was last down almost 1% at about $104 per barrel. West Texas Intermediate futures was little changed at around $96 per barrel.
 Election Day
 Investors are also focused on the midterm elections Tuesday, which will decide which party controls the House and Senate starting in January. Prediction market traders see a nearly 75% likelihood of Democrats taking the Senate .
 A sweep of the House and Senate by Democrats could weigh on the broader market on Wednesday — and spark a sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks especially — if investors haven't already positioned for that outcome. If Republicans keep control of the Senate or both chambers, the market may see short-term gains, JPMorgan said this week.
 Even with President Donald Trump in the White House, a victory by Democrats in either the House or Senate could shape investigations and oversight in Washington — key for industries including defense, AI and healthcare.
 Once the elections are over, it's possible the market may still move higher regardless of the outcome, according to Snyder at Potomac Fund. 
 "You're looking at an AI trade that's already taken a hit," he said. "That, combined with the idea that the uncertainty from the midterm fades, probably argues for relief rally no matter what."
 Correction: A prior version of this story had an incorrect forecast for Apple's first-quarter guidance. 
 10 Min Ago Information tech leads S&P 500 higher
 The S&P 500 information technology sector propelled the broad market index higher on Tuesday.
 In afternoon trading, the group was up 1.4%, the most of any S&P 500 sector on the day. The sector was followed by industrials, which rose 1.2%. Communication services also gained nearly 1%.
 Six of the 11 S&P 500 sectors saw losses, with materials and consumer staples leading the way there at a loss of 1.5% and 1.3%, respectively. 
 A look under the hood shows the S&P 500 had more laggards than gainers. 291 stocks were in the red, while 211 traded in positive territory.
 The broad market index was last up 0.5%.
 — Sean Conlon 
 1 Hour Ago Stocks making big moves: Coinbase, Shopify, Bloom Energy
 Here are some of the companies making headlines in midday trading: 
 Coinbase — The cryptocurrency exchange rallied 8% Tuesday after sliding 15% in the three trading days through Monday. Coinbase reported third-quarter results postmarket last Thursday showing weaker crypto trading volumes, leading Morgan Stanley to lower its rating to underweight and slash its price target by 53% Monday.
 Shopify — The e-commerce platform fell more than 5% Tuesday after the company missed estimates on subscription gross profit and gross merchandise volume. Overall, quarterly revenue came in at $3.74 billion, just below LSEG estimates of $3.75 billion. Shopify said it sees revenue growth in the "low thirties" range year over year for the fourth quarter, versus LSEG estimates of 32.1%. Shopify expects free cash flow margin to be consistent with the fourth quarter of 2025 .
 Bloom Energy — The maker of solid oxide fuel cells gained nearly 10% after Barclays upgraded Bloom to overweight from equal weight on Tuesday. The bank cited higher-than-expected demand, but lowered its 12-month price target to $289 from $319, which still implies upside of about 47% from Monday's close.
 Read here for the full list.
 — Ananya Chetia 
 2 Hours Ago Bill Ackman voices concern over ‘casino’ stock market
 Pershing Square CEO Bill Ackman speaks on CNBC's "Squawk Box," Nov. 3, 2026. CNBC Bill Ackman told CNBC on Tuesday he worries that the stock market is broken, saying the rise of speculative trading is leading to wild price swings thanks to the amount of leverage in the system.
 "Every number of days, I feel like markets are broken," Ackman said on CNBC's " Squawk Box ." "Stocks trade at prices that make no sense to me. Yes, it's good if you're a long-term investor and you can buy at a stupid price. I don't think it's good for the country generally."
 "We're back to the casino-type markets when there was 95% leverage," he added. "I don't think that's inherently good for the economy, for society, and it's leading to these massive moves in stocks."
 Read the full story here .
 — Sarah Min 
 4 Hours Ago A blue wave in the midterms could rattle the market
 Traffic lights are visible near the US Capitol is seen at sunrise in Washington, DC, November 3, 2026. Saul Loeb | Afp | Getty Images The stock market is not yet pricing in a Democratic sweep of Congress — despite some polls and most prediction markets pointing that way — so that scenario could weigh on share prices Wednesday, according to investors and analysts.
 Republicans managing to keep control could cause a short-term relief rally, they said.
 Short-term moves aside, the typical post-midterm pattern in the months ahead is bullish. But some wonder if the market could buck the positive historical trend this time because the S&P 500 is already up so much this year going into the election.
 As far as certain stocks to watch, a big Democratic win on Tuesday night — especially in the Texas governor race — could add fuel to an AI stock sell-off on the notion that more data center restrictions would gain momentum nationally. Defense stocks could come under pressure on fears of limits on spending. Read more .
 — Sean Conlon 
 4 Hours Ago Democratic success in midterms could send AI regulation jitters through markets, analyst says
 Advocates urge Hochul to slow down, expand the review process, and allow the public to meaningfully engage as the Public Service Commission meets as part of the review process for a data center moratorium on Wednesday, Oct. 28 2026, at the Empire State Plaza in Albany, N.Y. Lori Van Buren | Albany Times Union | Getty Images A strong showing from Democrats in Tuesday's midterm elections could go hand-in-hand with financial market jitters stemming from concerns about the regulation of AI, according to one top fixed income analyst.
 "The better the Democrats perform, the more nervous the market is likely to become regarding AI regulations," Ian Lyngen, head of U.S. rates strategy at BMO Capital Markets, said in Tuesday note to clients.
 Lyngen is expecting gridlock to result from the midterms – a situation in which one party controls one or both chambers of Congress, with the other party controlling the White House. This usually means that no large, programmatic policy changes can make it through the legal process, though smaller agreements and compromises usually can.
 "Even with this backdrop, and the price action of the last week, the equity market is holding up relatively well – all things considered," Lyngen said.
 Other analysts and commentators have made the opposite observation from Lyngen, saying that gridlock could actually be good for some technology companies, since it may help to preserve a legislative and regulatory status quo.
 Such conditions may be advantageous to frontier algorithm companies that are seeking competitive protections within the rapidly commodifying field of artificial intelligence.
 While Democratic success at the state and local level may pose obstacles for the physical data center buildout, it may be a good thing for industry at the federal level, Rob Rains at Washington Analysis told CNBC.
 "At the federal level, I would say that efforts to try to protect industry and to try to fence off [or] undercut Chinese competitors are likely to pick up considerably because that will be a huge priority for a Democratic Congress or a Democratic Senate," Rains said.
 He added: "It will put the President and the White House in a difficult spot because I think, given their druthers, they would rather not confront those issues at this time."
 — Tobias Burns 
 5 Hours Ago S&P 500, Nasdaq open higher
 The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite began Tuesday's session in the green.
 The tech-heavy Nasdaq gained 0.4%, while the broad market S&P 500 added 0.1%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, however, shed 188 points, or 0.4%.
 — Sean Conlon 
 5 Hours Ago U.S. crude oil moves below $95
 Crude oil prices fell Tuesday for a second consecutive session, as the market hopes the U.S. and Iran will reach a diplomatic settlement to the eight-month-long conflict that has disrupted global energy supplies.
 Brent crude was down 3% at $101.54 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate was 2.3% lower to $94.23. The move lower came after rumors circulated the U.S. and Iran were making progress toward a deal. Read more .
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon WTI, 1-day — Spencer Kimball 
 6 Hours Ago Buy the dip in Lumentum, Raymond James says
 Omar Marques | Lightrocket | Getty Images Shares of Lumentum sunk more than 18.5% on Monday after Marvell Technology announced a deal to acquire the company for $115 billion . But Raymond James thinks that sell-off is overdone. 
 The firm upgraded Lumentum to strong buy from outperform, and raised its price target to $1328. That implies a 94% gain from Monday's close. While some investors are skeptical about why Lumentum would sell itself now, analyst Simon Leopold outlined the reasoning in a Monday note. 
 "Lumentum's explanation is that the combined entity massively increases the TAM and provides RemainCo with the tech/tools needed to enable more design wins, differentiated products, and higher margins, which benefits shareholders willing to bet on the strategic vision," he wrote in the note. "Part of the assertion is that co-engineering improves the time-to-market, and we agree. A.I. hardware is evolving at breakneck speed, and winning long-term requires extreme co-design, as interconnect enables the next generation of scale compute."
 Lumentum was rebounding in premarket trading Tuesday, up 2%. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Lumentum 5-day. — Davis Giangiulio 
 6 Hours Ago Revvity, Pfizer and Zebra Technologies among the stocks making moves before the bell
 Check out the companies making the biggest moves premarket: 
 Revvity —  Shares gained 7% after the life sciences company raised its full-year pro forma adjusted earnings per share guidance to $5.40-$5.45 from a previous range of $5.30-$5.40.
 Pfizer — The pharma giant traded along the flatline after reporting its third-quarter results. Pfizer earned  87 cents per share, excluding certain items, on revenue of $16.58 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG expected a profit of 73 cents per share on revenue of $15.87 billion.
 Zebra Technologies — The maker of barcode scanners and mobile computers used in retail and other industries fell over 6% even after it reported better-than-expected third-quarter numbers. Zebra earned $4.95 per share, excluding certain items, on revenue of $1.61 billion. Analysts polled by FactSet expected a profit of $4.89 per share on revenue of $1.57 billion. To be sure, free cash flow guidance of at least $1 billion for the year was marginally below a $1.02 billion estimate.
 Read the full list here .
 — Ananya Chetia 
 7 Hours Ago Yum Brands slips after earnings
 Taco Bell logo sign is seen in New York City, United States, on August 6, 2026. Marcin Golba | Nurphoto | Getty Images Shares of Yum Brands were down by 0.5% despite reporting stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings. 
 The restaurant chain operator delivered adjusted earnings of $1.56 per share, compared to analysts polled by LSEG's estimates for $1.49 per share. Revenue came in-line with estimates at $2.05 billion. 
 Yum's same-store sales growth was weighed down by Taco Bell, which was impacted by a cyclospora outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce. But the company said Taco Bell had since rebounded. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Yum Brands 5-day chart. — Davis Giangiulio 
 9 Hours Ago Treasury yields move higher
 Treasury yields edged higher Tuesday as voting began in the U.S. midterm elections, while investors parse a busy week of economic data and renewed Middle East tensions that pushed oil prices higher.
 Yields on 10-year U.S. Treasurys — the main benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt —  rose more than 1 basis point to 4.9105%.
 The yield on longer-dated 30-year U.S. Treasurys — which tends to move more on geopolitical developments — was up 1 basis point at 5.2815%. 
 The yield on the 2-year Treasury note , which more closely follows short-term Federal Reserve rate decisions, was holding steady at 4.5915%. 
 — Hugh Leask 
 9 Hours Ago Bayer posts beat-and-raise quarter as pharma outperforms 
 Bill Anderson, CEO of Germany's drug maker Bayer AG, poses for a portrait session next to the company's logo at the Bayer headquarters in Leverkusen, Germany, December 10, 2024.  Wolfgang Rattay | Reuters Shares of Bayer jumped as much as 5.6% after the pharmaceutical and chemicals company posted quarterly results ahead of expectations and raised its full-year guidance. 
 Driven by its pharma business performance, Bayer said it now sees adjusted core earnings of between 9.8 billion euros and 10.3 billion euros (between $11 billion and $11.5 billion) on ​a currency-adjusted basis, up from a previously expected range of 9.6 billion euros and 10.1 billion euros.
 "We've reached a turning point in Pharma's growth trajectory and we're beginning to see the other side," said CEO Bill Anderson in a statement. Sales of its prostate cancer drug Nubeqa and kidney medicine Kerendia topped expectations in the quarter.
 In the third quarter, group sales amounted to 10.1 billion euros, up 1.9% on an adjusted basis. Core earnings rose 6.9% to 1.6 billion euros, 13.5% ahead of FactSet expectations, as the pharmaceutical business more than offset weakness in its crop science and consumer health businesses. 
 Bayer shares are up around 42% this year as the German conglomerate works to resolve U.S. litigation over its Roundup weedkiller , inherited through its 2018 Monsanto acquisition. Bayer denies claims that the product causes cancer and has paid more than $11 billion in legal costs.
 — Elsa Ohlen 
 10 Hours Ago Swiss inflation jumps to 1.5%
 Interlaken, Switzerland Laphon Pinta | Moment | Getty Images Switzerland's annual inflation rate reached a hotter-than-expected 1.5% in October, up from 1% the previous month. The rise was largely due to the rising cost of heating oil, petrol and diesel.
 Economists polled by Reuters had been expecting Swiss inflation to rise to 1.3% on an annual basis. 
 Switzerland's central bank has a target range for inflation of 0% to 2%. 
 The safe haven Swiss franc was 0.2% higher against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday morning. 
 — Chloe Taylor 
 10 Hours Ago Brookfield targets $27 billion AI data center at power station. Energy firm Drax surges 8%
 Brookfield is targeting a massive artificial intelligence data center in the north of England, as Europe scrambles to develop infrastructure to support the rollout of AI amid high energy and land costs.
 Energy company Drax Group said Tuesday it has signed an agreement with Brookfield and the asset manager's neocloud platform Radiant to jointly develop an AI data center on the Drax Power Station estate in North Yorkshire. London-listed shares of Drax were up 8.2% in early morning trading.
 Brookfield plans for a $27 billion AI data center at UK power station 11 Hours Ago European chip stocks tumble
 European semiconductor stocks fell in early trading amid a global technology sell-off. ASML fell by 3.4%, ASMI by 2.1%, STMicroelectronics by 3.9% and Infineon Tech by 3.9%.
 "I don't think this is a concern about current earnings because current earnings are strong. It's not a concern around the current cycle because we've just seen the [ U.S. ISM figures ] yesterday... the cycle is still doing well," Willem Sels, HSBC's chief investment officer, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Tuesday.
 "It's a wild ride. It's a concentrated ride as well, so whenever there is news around the AI cycle, people can take important decisions."
 "But it is mostly that mismatch between current spending and future revenues , you know, coming from the data centers. Now that's obviously quite characteristic for any new technology, and that's a fact of life. I do think that from a credit perspective, we're not seeing a broad-based sell-off at this point."
 "Ultimately, the demand for AI will continue to pick up exponentially in our view," he added.
 — Jenni Reid 
 11 Hours Ago European stock markets open lower 
 European stock markets opened broadly lower on Tuesday, with the regional Stoxx 600 index down 0.62% at the open. 
 Concerns over the financial health of technology firms continued to weigh, with the sector down 2.1%, while mining stocks fell 2.2%. 
 Food and beverage and healthcare stocks were the lone bright spots, both up around 0.3%. 
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Stoxx 600 index. — Jenni Reid 
 12 Hours Ago Asia markets end Tuesday mostly down
 Asia markets were mostly down on Tuesday, led by tech losses in South Korea and Taiwan.
 The Kospi ended 3.59% down at 5,648.79, while the small cap Kosdaq saw a larger loss of 4.08% to close at 704.39. The Taiwan Weighted Index also fell 3.59%, closing at 43,307.54. 
 Mainland China's CSI 300 closed 0.2% down at 4,008.87.
 The only exception was Australia's S&P/ASX 200 , which gained 0.34% to end at 8,886.8, as well as Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index , which was 0.37% up in its final hour of trade.
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 12 Hours Ago German auto parts maker Schaeffler to cut 3,460 jobs
 German car parts and machinery maker Schaeffler said Tuesday it would cut 3,460 jobs and close five of its sites across Europe, in the latest sign of strife in the European autos sector. 
 Approximately 2,660 jobs and four of the sites likely to be cut are in Germany. The company's performance improvement program is looking to eliminate overcapacity as it grapples with weaker demand for combustion engine vehicles and slower-than-expected pick-up of EVs.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Schaeffler share price. "Added to this are the above-average costs per employee in Germany and the high complexity of the organization, with too many management levels and overly limited delegation of leadership responsibilities," it said in a statement. 
 Schaeffler said it expected to incur one-off costs of 480 million euros ($537.2 million) and around a 400 million euros annual boost to earnings from 2030.
 Schaeffler also on Tuesday reported a 0.2% year-on-year fall in revenue to 5.8 billion euros in the third quarter, and a 7.2% fall in earnings before interest and taxes before special items to 245 million euros.
 Germany's Volkswagen is currently engaged in a massive strategic overhaul expected to result in around 100,000 job cuts.
 — Jenni Reid 
 15 Hours Ago Australia hikes rates to 18-year high to fight inflation
 Australia's central bank raised its benchmark cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85% on Tuesday, the highest level since November 2008.
 The Reserve Bank of Australia's move was in line with expectations from economists polled by Reuters, and marked its fifth rate increase this year.
 This also comes as the country continues to grapple with high inflation, with the consumer price index rising 4.3% in September, up from 4% in August and marking its highest level since March.
 The central bank also said inflation is now expected to "remain elevated through much of 2027," and not expected to fall back into its 2%-3% target range till late 2027, three quarters later than previously forecast.
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 16 Hours Ago North Korea denies links to Binance hack as researchers trace stolen billions
 Visual China Group | Getty Images North Korea rejected U.S. allegations linking Pyongyang to the estimated $6.3 billion Binance hack, calling the accusation a "grave political provocation," according to state media.
 Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denounced the FBI's attribution of the attack to North Korea-linked hacking group TraderTraitor, Yohnap reported Tuesday, citing the state-run Korean Central News Agency.
 She accused Washington of misleading international public opinion by portraying cybercrimes around the world as the work of North Korea.
 — Jenny Lee 
 18 Hours Ago Hong Kong inches up in early trade, China slips
 Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index rose 0.16% in early trade in Asia, with gains in the academic and education sector offsetting losses from the energy sector.
 Mainland China, on the other hand, saw the CSI 300 index slip 0.84%, also weighed down by tech and energy stocks.
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 19 Hours Ago South Korea tracks tech losses on Wall Street, Australia holds up
 Asia-Pacific markets were mixed early Tuesday, with South Korea's Kospi sliding sharply as it tracked Wall Street's losses in the tech sector.
 The Kospi dropped 3.55% at open, with heavyweight Samsung Electronics down by 5%, while the small-cap Kosdaq slipped 2.53%. 
 Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 was 0.21% higher.
 —Lim Hui Jie 
 20 Hours Ago Stocks making the biggest moves in extended trading: Apple, Clorox, Palantir & more
 Several stocks made sharp moves in after-hours trading following the latest round of earnings releases.
 Apple — Apple shares were down 2% in extended trading after the consumer tech giant rolled out a disappointing margin forecast and iPad sales in the fiscal fourth quarter missed the Street's estimates.
 The Clorox Company — The maker of Clorox Disinfecting Wipes added 2% after fiscal first-quarter results came in ahead of estimates. The company earned $1.55 per share on an adjusted basis on revenue of $1.91 billion. Analysts surveyed by LSEG were looking for $1.07 a share and $1.88 billion. Organic sales growth for the period also topped estimates.
 Palantir Technologies — Palantir shares were down 2% even after the company's third-quarter earnings topped Wall Street's estimates. Revenue for the period nearly doubled from a year earlier and surpassed $2 billion for the first time. The company's U.S. commercial revenue jumped 148% to $984 million, topping U.S. government revenue of $953 million. Palantir is also projecting about $2.65 billion in fourth-quarter revenue and $8.53 billion for full-year 2026.
 Read more about Monday evening's movers here .
 Correction: A prior version of this blog post had an incorrect forecast for Apple's first-quarter guidance. 
 — Darla Mercado 
 20 Hours Ago Asia markets set for higher open as investors look to midterms
 Asia-Pacific markets were set to open higher Tuesday, breaking ranks with the tech induced slide on Wall Street as investors also looked toward the U.S. midterm elections.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 started the day 0.57% higher as traders awaited the Reserve Bank of Australia's rate decision later on Tuesday.
 Hong Kong  Hang Seng index  futures were at 23,535, compared with the index's last close of 23,393.
 Japan's markets are closed for a public holiday.
 — Lim Hui Jie 
 20 Hours Ago Stock futures are flat as investors weigh Apple earnings and U.S. midterm elections loom
 Nasdaq-100 futures were little changed after 6 p.m. in New York.
 Dow Jones Industrial Average futures lost 0.02%. S&P 500 futures fell 0.02%. Nasdaq-100 futures added 0.09%.
 — Deena Zaidi
